riparian_buffer__asset_threat__flood.mechanism: Flood disturbance can break, buckle or uproot buffer plants, and plants with more flexible stems resist and recover better [ev_flood_hazard_cole20_3]. In a US multispecies riparian buffer, willow posts withstood the intense 1993 flooding and caught large logs and bridge planks, although some stems were skinned and did not resprout [ev_flood_hazard_schultz95_3].

riparian_buffer__biodiversity_priority.mechanism: Buffers reduce sediments and contaminants reaching watercourses, favouring pollution-sensitive mayflies, stoneflies and caddisflies over tolerant chironomids, and in Brazil indicator fish and aquatic invertebrates decline abruptly as native riparian vegetation is lost, especially close to the stream [ev_biodiversity_outcome_cole20_4, ev_biodiversity_outcome_dalacorte20_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_dalacorte20_4, ev_biodiversity_outcome_dalacorte20_6]. riparian_buffer__biodiversity_priority.conditionality: The evidence pools opposite and null findings: botanical-diversity evidence is conflicting, plant richness was similar across buffer widths, small mammals did not differ by buffer width, planted species often failed to establish, and bird density and richness were lower in buffer strips than in undisturbed shore forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_cole20_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_cole20_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_8, ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_9, ev_biodiversity_outcome_gonzalez15_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_5]. The UK review units cite earlier studies and the Iowa runoff unit enters as a component of flood impact; only the Iowa unit comes from rainfed cropping, and all units are high-income evidence [ev_flood_hazard_cole20_1, ev_runoff_reduction_schultz95_1].

riparian_buffer__planted__flood_hazard.mechanism: Wooded buffers slow the flow of water from the land into receiving water bodies by increasing infiltration, reducing flow velocity and providing temporary water storage [ev_flood_hazard_cole20_1]. Mature riparian woodland is described as more effective because of its greater structural complexity and the larger volume of deadwood entering watercourses [ev_flood_hazard_cole20_2].
riparian_buffer__planted__flood_hazard.conditionality: The benefit is described for moderate flooding and depends on woodland extent, location, age and density, so young planted woodland may not deliver it [ev_flood_hazard_cole20_2]. Both units are cited secondary statements in one UK review (high-income, temperate Europe), outside the LIC/LMIC target [ev_flood_hazard_cole20_1, ev_flood_hazard_cole20_2].

riparian_buffer__planted__soil_erosion_r.mechanism: Grass filter strips trap sediment carried in runoff: an 8-m strip reduced sediment loss by 97%, a 9-m fescue strip by 99%, and fescue and switchgrass-barrier strips both reduced it by 91% within 4 m [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_2, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_4]. A dense switchgrass zone stops concentrated flow from fields and lets water infiltrate well above the field rate [ev_runoff_reduction_schultz95_1]. Trees planted in buffers stabilise river banks, and at a US site only an additional 0.3 m of bank was lost after willow posts were installed [ev_streambank_erosion_cole20_1, ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_1, ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_2].
riparian_buffer__planted__soil_erosion_r.conditionality: The cell rests on proxy/component evidence (sediment retention, runoff and bank erosion) rather than direct measurement of soil erosion risk, which is why its class is capped [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_runoff_reduction_schultz95_1, ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_1]. Results depend on texture and setting: 4-m grass buffers trapped almost 100% of sandy loam but only 35% of silty clay loam, and the forestry-harvest units on buffer width, including 30-m buffers that did not prevent sedimentation after clearcutting, concern retained forest rather than planted strips [ev_sediment_retention_cole20_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_3]. All units are from the USA, Canada and the UK (high income), outside the LIC/LMIC target [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_1, ev_streambank_erosion_cole20_1].

riparian_buffer__planted__water_quality_.mechanism: Grass filter strips reduce sediment and nutrient losses in runoff: an 8-m strip reduced sediment loss by 97%, a 9-m fescue strip by 99%, and organic N and nitrate losses past 8 m of fescue were lower than on cultivated fallow [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_1, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_3]. Grass and forest buffer strips achieved 80% to 90% nitrate reduction in subsurface water, and nitrate-nitrogen in a US multispecies buffer never exceeded 2 mg/l against more than 12 mg/l in adjacent fields [ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_2, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_1]. Wooded buffers shade streams, damping diel temperature fluctuations and limiting temperature rise after harvest [ev_stream_temperature_cole20_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_2, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_3].
riparian_buffer__planted__water_quality_.conditionality: Wooded buffers removed nitrate from shallow groundwater better than grass buffers but phosphates less well, and their nutrient-removal effectiveness typically diminishes as trees age [ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_4, ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_7]. Sediment trapping depends on texture (almost 100% of sandy loam but only 35% of silty clay loam in 4-m grass buffers), and the forestry-harvest units, including 30-m buffers that did not prevent sedimentation after clearcutting, concern retained forest rather than planted strips [ev_sediment_retention_cole20_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_3]. All units are from the USA, Canada and the UK (high income), outside the LIC/LMIC target [ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_1, ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_4].

riparian_buffer__soil_erosion_risk.mechanism: Grass filter strips trap sediment carried in runoff: an 8-m strip reduced sediment loss by 97%, a 9-m fescue strip by 99% and a 4.6-m strip retained 83%, with trapping efficiency rising sharply over the first 10 m and then tailing off [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_2, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_3, ev_sediment_retention_cole20_1]. Trees planted in buffers stabilise river banks: at a US site only an additional 0.3 m of bank was lost after willow posts were installed, and a reach with restored grass and herbaceous cover kept its integrity through the 1993 floods [ev_streambank_erosion_cole20_1, ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_1, ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_2]. In Brazil more riparian forest correlates with lower suspended solids, and replacing riparian forest with other cover increases bank erosion [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2, ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11].
riparian_buffer__soil_erosion_risk.conditionality: The cell rests on proxy/component evidence (sediment retention, runoff and bank erosion) rather than direct measurement of soil erosion risk on farmland, which is why its class is capped [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_1]. Effectiveness depends on sediment and setting: 4-m grass buffers trapped almost 100% of sandy loam but only 35% of silty clay loam, and 30-m buffers did not prevent stream sedimentation after partial clearcutting [ev_sediment_retention_cole20_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_2]. Evidence is mainly from the USA, Canada and the UK (high income), with Brazil and Mexico (upper-middle), so it is outside the LIC/LMIC target, and the Brazilian bank-erosion unit is loss-based (erosion as forest is lost) [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_cole20_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5, ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11].

riparian_buffer__soil_erosion_risk__inco.mechanism: In a Brazilian basin, more riparian forest correlates with lower total and organic suspended solids in streams, and riparian forest is cited as reducing sediment loading [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_10]. Mexican farmers identify tree roots as preventing riverbank erosion during floods, and replacing riparian forest with other land cover increases bank erosion and sediment loads [ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5, ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11]. Properly designed buffers are asserted to trap and remove sediments from runoff [ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1].
riparian_buffer__soil_erosion_risk__inco.conditionality: The units are correlations, citations, a farmer perception, an uncited assertion and a loss-based statement, so none measures an erosion reduction from a buffer [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_10, ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1, ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11]. Recorded contexts are Brazil and Mexico (upper-middle income), with one assertion lacking context; this matches the scope row but is not LIC/LMIC evidence [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1].

riparian_buffer__water_quality_risk.mechanism: Grass filter strips reduce sediment and nutrient losses in runoff, with organic N and nitrate losses past 8 m of fescue lower than on cultivated fallow, and grass and forest buffer strips achieved 80% to 90% nitrate reduction in subsurface water [ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_1, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_3, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_2]. Nitrate-nitrogen in a US multispecies buffer never exceeded 2 mg/l against more than 12 mg/l in adjacent fields, and wooded buffers shade streams, damping diel temperature fluctuations and limiting temperature rise after harvest [ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_1, ev_stream_temperature_cole20_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_3]. In Brazil, more riparian forest correlates with lower nitrogen, phosphorus, faecal coliforms and suspended solids and with higher dissolved oxygen [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_4, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_5, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_6, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1].
riparian_buffer__water_quality_risk.conditionality: Findings are not uniform: widening buffers from 4 to 8 m did not reduce soluble herbicide loadings, a meta-analysis found no effect of width on nitrogen removal, nutrient-saturated buffers can become a nutrient source, and 30-m buffers did not prevent sedimentation after clearcutting [ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_1, ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_3, ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_6, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_2]. Much of the cell rests on components (sediment retention, stream temperature) and on Brazilian correlations, citations and assertions rather than measured water-quality change after buffer establishment [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_3, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_1]. Evidence is from the USA, Canada and the UK (high income) and Brazil (upper-middle), plus statements with no recorded context, so it is outside the LIC/LMIC target [ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_1, ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_1, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_3, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_2].

riparian_buffer__water_quality_risk__inc.mechanism: In a Brazilian basin, more riparian forest correlates with lower nitrogen, phosphorus, faecal coliforms and suspended solids and with higher dissolved oxygen, and the riparian forest raised dissolved oxygen more than forest across the whole watershed [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_4, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_5, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_6, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_7, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2]. Riparian forest is cited as reducing nitrate, phosphorus and sediment loading, riparian vegetation as critical for mitigating nitrate pollution, and the authors conclude that riparian restoration can be prioritised as a short-term action to improve water quality [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_9, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_12, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_8]. Properly designed buffers are asserted to trap and remove nutrients and sediments, with wider buffers likely more effective though gains slow with width [ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_1, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_3, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_4, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_2, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_5, ev_nutrient_removal_meli19_3].
riparian_buffer__water_quality_risk__inc.conditionality: The evidence is correlational, cited or asserted, with no measured before-after or buffer-versus-no-buffer change, and one cited statement concerns forest buffers between urban areas and streams rather than farmland [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_9, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_1, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_5]. Only Brazil (upper-middle income) is recorded on the units; the remaining statements have no recorded country, so this matches the scope row but is not LIC/LMIC evidence [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_3, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_2, ev_nutrient_removal_meli19_3].
